bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 10676: open62541 has a reported heap-use-after-free (READ 8). Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8. Crash State: UA_WorkQueue_manuallyProcessDelayed / UA_WorkQueue_cleanup / UA_Server_delete. The AFL fuzz target fuzz_binary_message feeds a raw OPC UA binary message stream that creates a session (and subscription); on server shutdown/delete the delayed-callback work queue dereferences an already-freed session-embedded callback node.

source.code: retval = UA_decodeBinary(msg, &offset, request, requestType, server->config.customDataTypesSize, server->config.customDataTypes);
source.description: The untrusted OPC UA binary MSG chunk is decoded into a concrete service request; a CreateSessionRequest decoded here drives materialization of the session object that later becomes the dangling object read at the sink.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled OPC UA binary message stream `msg` supplied to the fuzz_binary_message target and assembled by the SecureChannel; decoded into `request` (e.g. UA_CreateSessionRequest).

sink.description: On the second work-queue cleanup pass (reached from UA_Server_delete), the delayed-callback list is iterated and SIMPLEQ_FOREACH_SAFE reads dc->next from a session-embedded delayed-callback node that was already freed during the run_shutdown cleanup pass: ASan heap-use-after-free READ of size 8.

root_cause.description: removeSession schedules a delayed free of the session_list_entry (the embedded cleanupCallback lives at offset 0 of the entry) WITHOUT first synchronously closing the session's subscriptions. Subscription teardown is instead deferred into UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup, which runs late as the removeSessionCallback delayed callback. Deleting subscriptions at that point (during the same manuallyProcessDelayed pass that frees the session at ua_workqueue.c:255) leaves delayed-callback nodes tied to the freed session in the queue, so a later cleanup pass dereferences freed memory. The fix (commit 2177132) moves subscription/publish-queue teardown into removeSession so subscriptions are closed synchronously before the SecureChannel is detached and before the delayed session free is scheduled.

parser_admitted.description: The reassembled OPC UA message has passed SecureChannel chunk framing/dispatch and is admitted into the MSG service handler (processMSG), i.e. attacker input has cleared transport/container dispatch and entered the target service-processing path that materializes the session.

tainted_value_origin.description: The 368-byte session_list_entry allocated in response to the attacker's CreateSessionRequest. This object (with the delayed cleanupCallback embedded at offset 0) is the heap region that is freed at ua_workqueue.c:255 and then re-read at ua_workqueue.c:251.

coarse_trace.summary: Decodes and dispatches an attacker-controlled OPC UA service request (CreateSession) from the binary MSG chunk.
Allocates the session_list_entry that becomes the dangling object.
Schedules a delayed free of the session without first closing its subscriptions synchronously.
run_shutdown cleanup pass runs the session cleanup callback and frees the session_list_entry.
UA_Server_delete triggers a second cleanup pass that dereferences the freed session-embedded callback node.

fine_trace.code: retval = UA_decodeBinary(msg, &offset, request, requestType, server->config.customDataTypesSize, server->config.customDataTypes);
fine_trace.note: Untrusted OPC UA MSG chunk `msg` is decoded into a service request; a CreateSessionRequest here initiates creation of the session object that later dangles.
The decoded CreateSessionRequest is dispatched to the CreateSession service handler.
The service handler forwards the request to the session manager to allocate a session.
ASan allocation site: the 368-byte session_list_entry. Its cleanupCallback member sits at offset 0, so freeing that callback later frees the whole entry.

When the session is removed (channel close / CloseSession during message processing) the embedded delayed cleanup callback is armed to point back at the session entry; the session memory is not freed yet, only scheduled.

ROOT CAUSE: the delayed session free is enqueued WITHOUT first closing the session's subscriptions synchronously. Subscription teardown is deferred into the delayed UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup, so subscription-related delayed callbacks tied to the session survive past the session free. The fix closes subscriptions here in removeSession before detaching the SecureChannel.
Server shutdown runs the first delayed-callback cleanup pass over the work queue.

The delayed cleanup callback deletes the session members INCLUDING its subscriptions at this late point; deleting subscriptions leaves/enqueues further delayed callbacks bound to the session that is about to be freed.
ASan free site: after the callback returns, the session entry (dc == &sentry->cleanupCallback, offset 0 of the session_list_entry) is freed during the run_shutdown cleanup pass.

After run_shutdown already freed the session in its cleanup pass, UA_Server_delete triggers a SECOND work-queue cleanup pass over the delayed-callback list that still references the freed session node.
SINK: the second cleanup pass iterates the delayed-callback list and dereferences dc->next on the freed session-embedded callback node -> heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at ua_workqueue.c:251.

format.name: OPC UA binary message stream (open62541 fuzz_binary_message)
format.contract: Candidate input must be a sequence of OPC UA binary transport chunks (HEL/OPN/MSG) that pass SecureChannel chunk framing and reach the MSG service dispatch (processMSG), successfully creating a session via CreateSession and attaching subscription state, and then driving session/SecureChannel teardown so that at server shutdown+delete the delayed-callback work queue is processed twice over a session-embedded callback node. Reachability-comparable PoCs must preserve parser-admission through UA_SecureChannel_processCompleteMessages and processMSG and the session+subscription lifecycle that leaves a delayed callback referencing freed session memory.
